chains.title: FLI1 binding at the alt allele alters IRF6 dosage in oral epithelium

links.claim: FLI1 has its own QBiC-SELEX model: the alt G allele is predicted to bind more strongly than ref A (z 13.73, effect +0.906; alt 98.7th vs ref 90.1st percentile). ENCODE has no FLI1 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in any biosample, and FLI1 expression in GTEx minor salivary gland is modest (8.27 TPM, 51.9th percentile), so occupancy at this base is not established.
The variant lies in EH38E2863563, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac marks, consistent with an active enhancer.
IRF6 is the nearest TSS, 9.7 kb away, and is a cleft-lip L2G gene; IRF6 also has a brain eQTL at this variant (alt G NES -0.62), but no enhancer-target assay or oral epithelial eQTL is given.

FLI1 is expressed in GTEx minor salivary gland, a craniofacial/secretory tissue, but no oral epithelial expression, matched ENCODE biosample, or ChIP data are provided, so the cell-type link remains inferred.

The cleft GWAS association is weak (p 2e-6) and its effect allele is A; the IRF6 brain eQTL has alt G lowering IRF6. A simple alt-G/FLI1-to-IRF6 cleft model therefore has unresolved or opposite direction and needs oral-cell functional evidence.

predictions: Allele-specific FLI1 ChIP enrichment at the alt G allele in oral epithelial cells.
Ref/alt reporter shows the alt G allele changes enhancer activity and IRF6 expression in oral epithelial cells.
The effect depends on the Ets motif.

The alt G allele does not change enhancer activity or IRF6 expression in oral epithelial cells.

chains.title: ETV2-like Ets binding at the alt allele affects UTP25

links.claim: ETV2 has no independent QBiC-SELEX model at this site; the prediction uses a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 Ets model, which favors the alt G allele (z 77.65, effect +1.32). ETV2 occupancy is unknown because ENCODE never assayed ETV2 here, so this is not ETV2-specific evidence.
The variant is in EH38E2863563, a dELS with active enhancer marks.
UTP25 is 12 kb from the variant and has the highest L2G score (0.75), but there is no UTP25 eQTL or enhancer-target assay; literature search hits are not direct functional evidence.
An ETV2-driven mechanism would require ETV2 expression in craniofacial epithelial or endothelial cells; expression and occupancy are not shown in this case.
Altered UTP25 dosage in craniofacial cells could contribute to cleft lip, but the cleft association is weak and indirect, and no UTP25 dosage or functional enhancer evidence is provided.

chains.title: ZNF687 occupancy at the variant has a weak allele-specific effect

links.claim: ZNF687 has the only ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant, in GM12878. Its own QBiC-SELEX model shows a tiny ref-favoring change below the gate (z -0.21, effect -0.013) and a weak site, so allele-specific ZNF687 binding is not established.
The variant lies in the EH38E2863563 dELS active enhancer-like element.
IRF6 is the nearest TSS and a cleft-lip L2G gene, but no ZNF687-IRF6 target evidence is given.
The only direct occupancy evidence is in GM12878 lymphoblastoid cells, which are not the disease-relevant craniofacial cell type.
A ZNF687-mediated effect on IRF6 and cleft lip is possible but weak, because the allelic QBiC effect is negligible and the disease-relevant cell type is not matched.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr1:209815925:A>G, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (none: expression filter skipped), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 1 of 1 occupied (0 with a strong site), 5 of 249 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 0 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 572 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element. No occupied TF has a strong site at the variant.
